subject: computing
title: KS3 Computing — Data Compression
subtitle: Lossy and lossless compression techniques, including run-length encoding.

data.targetWord: the process of encoding data so that it takes up less storage space than the original

examples.en-GB: Compression is used to reduce the size of video files so they can be streamed over the internet quickly.

data.targetWord: a compression method that permanently removes some data from a file; the original cannot be fully restored after decompression

examples.en-GB: JPEG uses lossy compression, so saving a photo at low quality permanently removes fine detail.

data.targetWord: a compression method that reduces file size while preserving every bit of the original data; the file can be perfectly restored on decompression

examples.en-GB: ZIP uses lossless compression, so the decompressed file is identical to the original.

data.targetWord: a lossless compression algorithm that replaces consecutive repeated values with a count followed by the value (e.g. AAAA becomes 4A)

examples.en-GB: Run-length encoding compressed the row AAAABBBCC into 4A3B2C, saving 3 bytes.

data.targetWord: the ratio of the compressed file size to the original file size; a lower ratio indicates more effective compression

examples.en-GB: An encoded file of 6 bytes from an original of 10 bytes gives a compression ratio of 0.6 (60% of original).

data.targetWord: the amount of storage space a file occupies, measured in bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, or larger units

examples.en-GB: Compression reduced the file size of the video from 500 MB to 50 MB.

data.targetWord: a common lossy image file format best suited to photographs; achieves high compression by removing image detail the human eye is less sensitive to

examples.en-GB: Saving a holiday photo as a JPEG at 80% quality reduces the file size significantly with minimal visible loss.

data.targetWord: a common lossless image file format suited to graphics, logos, and screenshots; preserves all pixel data exactly

examples.en-GB: The school logo was saved as a PNG to ensure the sharp edges and exact colours were perfectly preserved.

data.targetWord: a common lossy audio file format that compresses sound by removing frequencies the human ear is least sensitive to

examples.en-GB: An MP3 of a 4-minute song is typically around 4 MB compared to 40 MB for the uncompressed WAV file.

data.targetWord: a common lossless archive file format used to compress one or more files of any type; no data is lost during compression

examples.en-GB: The teacher compressed all the worksheets into a ZIP file before emailing them to the class.

data.targetWord: a common lossy video container format that uses heavy compression to store video and audio; widely used for streaming

examples.en-GB: Streaming services encode films as MP4 files using lossy compression to reduce bandwidth usage.

data.targetWord: software that encodes or decodes a digital data stream; used to compress and decompress audio and video files

examples.en-GB: The H.264 codec is used to compress video in many MP4 files, making them small enough to stream online.

data.targetWord: repeated or unnecessary data in a file that can be removed or replaced to reduce file size without significant loss of information

examples.en-GB: RLE exploits redundancy in images by replacing long runs of the same colour pixel with a count and value.

data.targetWord: the process of converting data into a compressed or alternative format for storage or transmission

examples.en-GB: Encoding the pixel row AAAABBBCC using RLE produces 4A3B2C, reducing the data from 9 to 6 characters.

data.targetWord: the process of converting compressed or encoded data back into its original or usable form

examples.en-GB: Decoding the RLE sequence 3W2B1W restores the original string WWWBBW.

data.targetWord: a visual or audible distortion introduced into a file by lossy compression, such as blurriness or blockiness in an image

examples.en-GB: Saving the JPEG at very low quality introduced blocky artefacts around the edges of the text in the image.

data.targetWord: the permanent degradation of data fidelity that occurs when lossy compression removes information from a file

examples.en-GB: Each time the JPEG was re-saved at reduced quality, further quality loss accumulated until the image was barely recognisable.

data.targetWord: the ability to fully recover the exact original data from a compressed file; only possible with lossless compression

examples.en-GB: Because ZIP is lossless, full restoration of every original byte is guaranteed when the file is decompressed.

data.targetWord: the decrease in the amount of data needed to represent the same information, achieved through compression techniques

examples.en-GB: RLE achieves data reduction by replacing repeated values with a single count-value pair.

data.targetWord: the level of quality as experienced by a human observer; lossy compression exploits limitations in human perception to remove data that is unlikely to be noticed

examples.en-GB: MP3 compression targets perceptual quality by removing audio frequencies that humans struggle to hear.

data.targetWord: the structure and encoding method used to store data in a file, indicated by its extension (e.g. .jpg, .png, .mp3)

examples.en-GB: The file format determines whether an image is stored using lossy or lossless compression.

data.targetWord: the capacity to retain data on a device such as a hard drive, SSD, or cloud service; compression helps reduce the storage space required

examples.en-GB: Compressing the image files freed up 2 GB of storage on the laptop's hard drive.

data.targetWord: the maximum rate at which data can be transmitted over a network connection, usually measured in megabits per second (Mbps)

examples.en-GB: Compressing video files reduces bandwidth usage, allowing smooth streaming even on slower internet connections.

data.targetWord: the rate at which data is sent from one location to another; smaller compressed files transmit more quickly than large uncompressed files

examples.en-GB: Compressing the attachment from 20 MB to 5 MB greatly increased its transmission speed as an email.

data.targetWord: a situation where gaining one benefit requires accepting a disadvantage; in compression, smaller file size may mean lower quality or inability to restore the original

examples.en-GB: Using lossy compression involves a trade-off: you gain a much smaller file but lose the ability to recover the exact original data.

data.sentence: Lossy compression permanently ____ some data from a file, so the original cannot be fully recovered.
Lossless compression preserves ____ of the original data, so the file can be perfectly restored.
Run-length encoding replaces a run of repeated values with a ____ followed by the value.
JPEG is a ____ image format; saving a photograph as a JPEG permanently removes some detail.
PNG is a ____ image format; the decompressed image is pixel-for-pixel identical to the original.
ZIP is a ____ archive format, meaning all original file data is retained after decompression.
MP3 is a ____ audio format that removes frequencies the human ear is least sensitive to.
Lossy compression must ____ be used on program files because even a single changed bit can cause the program to crash.
Compression reduces ____ size, which means files can be stored more efficiently and sent more quickly over a network.
RLE is only efficient when data contains long ____ of repeated values; on complex photographs it can make the file larger.
Using RLE on 'ABCDE' produces '1A1B1C1D1E', which is ____ than the original — showing RLE can make files bigger.
The two main reasons to compress data are to save ____ space and to improve transmission speed.
Encoding the string WWWWBBBBWW using RLE gives 4W4B2W, saving ____ bytes compared to the original 10 bytes.
A visual distortion in a JPEG caused by heavy lossy compression — such as blockiness around edges — is called a compression ____.
A text file compressed with lossy compression might change a word or number, so ____ compression must always be used for text.
Decoding the RLE sequence 3W2B1W gives the original string ____.
The compression ____ is the ratio of the compressed size to the original size; a ratio of 0.6 means the file is 60% of its original size.
Medical images such as X-rays must use ____ compression to ensure no diagnostic information is ever lost.
Each time a JPEG file is re-saved at reduced quality, more quality is permanently lost — this is known as ____ loss.
RLE works by identifying and compressing consecutive runs of the same ____ in a data sequence.

data.title: Applying RLE to AAAABBBCC
data.instruction: Put the steps for encoding AAAABBBCC using run-length encoding in the correct order.
items: Identify the first run: four consecutive A values
Write the count and value for the first run: 4A
Identify the second run: three consecutive B values
Write the count and value for the second run: 3B
Identify the third run: two consecutive C values
Write the count and value for the third run: 2C
The complete RLE encoding is: 4A 3B 2C (6 bytes vs original 9 bytes)

data.title: Comparing File Sizes Before and After RLE
data.instruction: Put these steps for calculating bytes saved by RLE compression in the correct order.
items: Count the total number of characters in the original data string
Apply RLE to the data to produce the encoded sequence
Count the total number of characters in the encoded sequence
Subtract the encoded length from the original length
The result is the number of bytes saved by RLE compression
Calculate the compression ratio: encoded length divided by original length
